metas.name: American Samoa - Unique car
metas.note: If you see a Street View car with a slightly rusted black truck bed, you know you're in American Samoa.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Andorra - Stone buildings
metas.note:
Andorra has a lot of these distinct stone buildings, visible almost everywhere in the country.

These buildings can also be found near Andorra, in the French and Spanish Pyrenees.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/andorra for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Chevrons
metas.note:
Argentina typically uses white-and-red chevrons.

NOTE: Argentina is the only country in the Americas with these chevrons.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/argentina.

metas.name: Argentina - Double concrete pole
metas.note: This double-rounded concrete pole connected by a concrete ring is almost exclusive to Argentina. Similar ones can occasionally be found in Bolivia, but the landscape will be vastly different.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Highway markers
metas.note: If you see black-and-white highway markers, you're in Argentina.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - Landscape + black car
metas.note:
If you find yourself in a flat, desolate, treeless, sparsely populated area with a visible black back of the Google car, you're likely in Argentina.

(Jordan might resemble this landscape for new players, and it also has a black back on the car, so be aware of that.)

(Only other countries in South America with car like that are: Peru and Uruguay)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Argentina - License plate
metas.note: Old license plates in Argentina have a black dot in the middle of a white plate, which is easy to spot. New license plates are fully white with a blue line at the top, similar to those in Brazil.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/argentina for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - ACT gap reflector
metas.note:
If you see gap and reflector in between outer lines you gonna be in ACT.

(South Australia might have gaps in outerlines but reflector in a gap is super rare there)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - Bollard
metas.note:
Australian bollards are white with a red reflector on the front and grey on the back.

Turkish bollards are similar but lack a back reflector. If unsure, check the sun position, landscape, or vegetation.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - Give way sign
metas.note: Give-way signs in Australia have a white border and black text, while in New Zealand, they have red text.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - NSW guardrail ending
metas.note: Guardrail ending, featuring a black dash on a yellow background, is almost exclusive to New South Wales and the ACT.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - NSW red no stopping sign
metas.note: New South Wales is the only state to use red ‘No Stopping’ signs.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - NSW yellow plates.
metas.note: If you see more than couple yellow plates in Australia you should be in NSW
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - NT pole
metas.note: Rusty metal holey poles are unique to Northern Territory state in Australia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - QLD black paint
metas.note: These black markings are specific to electricity poles in Queensland(from Gold Coast to Sunshine Coast). They are often accompanied by diagonal numbers.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - QLD non south-east pole marking
metas.note: If you see this grayish long thin plate with numbers, sometimes with extra blue(or other color) little circle marking you gonna be in QLD(not in south east most likely because they use different marking).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - SA flat sign posts
metas.note: You can only find flat signposts in South Australia and Western Australia (in WA they mostly will be yellow but not always). You will also find rounded sign posts in SA (so don't rule SA if you see rounded one).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - SA property markers
metas.note: You can find these white property markers on the sides of roads in South Australia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - SA stobie pole
metas.note: The iconic Stobie pole, made of steel and concrete, is specific to South Australia.(A few thousand of these poles can be found in other states, most notably Tasmania - super rare)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - Tasmania pole metas
metas.note:
Metas for Tasmiania poles:

  • Olive-green possum guards
  • 90 degrees bend crossbar
  • this unique lamp arms
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - Vic pole top
metas.note: Victorian pole tops feature 3 circular coils; 2 on the sides, and 1 vertical one at the top.(sometimes might be missing the top one)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - Victoria hydrant bollard
metas.note: You can find these white hydrant poles that feature a blue circle and a red section on top of it in Victoria.(they have couple different designs but they all follow same color/shape +/- pattern)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - WA bollard
metas.note: Bollards with brown paint at the bottom are most commonly found in Western Australia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - wa pole metas
metas.note:
Western Australia pole metas:

  • Trident pole top(can also be seen in Victoria)
  • Green painted bottom of poles
  • red/white sticker
  • yellow horizontal sticker
  • white and gray sticker
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - WA property marker
metas.note: You can find these dark green property markers on the sides of roads in Western Australia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/australia.

metas.name: Australia - WA stripy bollard
metas.note: Black-and-white stripy bollards are unique to Western Australia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Australia - WA yellow sign posts
metas.note: Yellow signposts are specific to Western Australia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/australia for more clues.

metas.name: Austria - Bollard
metas.note:
Austria's bollards are white with a black top and dark red or grey reflectors, often featuring a nipple-shaped black cap and sometimes a snow pole.

Slovenia’s bollards are similar but always have a white back reflector, whereas in Austria, white reflectors are rare but possible.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/austria.

metas.name: Bangladesh - Language
metas.note: The Bengali script features a continuous horizontal line at the top of each word. It resembles Devanagari (Hindi) but can be recognized by the many letters with triangular shapes. Bengali is an official language in Bangladesh and parts of eastern India(but coverage there is taken with "shit cam")
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bangladesh.

metas.name: Belgium - Reddish license plates
metas.note: Belgian license plates should have a red tint visible through the blur because they use red text on a white license plate.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/belgium for more clues.

metas.name: Bermuda - Unique car
metas.note: If you see a black Street View car with the entire front side of the vehicle visible, you're in Bermuda.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Bhutan - Architecture
metas.note: Traditional Bhutanese architecture is very distinct. Most houses feature tin roofs and wooden painted frames, giving them a unique look.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bhutan.

metas.name: Bhutan - Red license plate
metas.note: License plates in Bhutan are almost always red and are easily visible on vehicles.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bhutan.

metas.name: Bhutan - Stone blocks guardrail
metas.note: Bhutan commonly uses stone blocks as safety barriers on winding rural roads. These blocks are very common and are one of the best ways to recognize rural roads in Bhutan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bhutan.

metas.name: Bolivia - Curvy poles
metas.note: Many wooden utility poles, particularly in the eastern parts of Bolivia are noticeably curvy and appear to be made from locally sourced tree trunks.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bolivia for more clues.

metas.name: Botswana - Vibes
metas.note:
A dry, flat landscape with African vegetation, usually a bit away from the road, is a good clue for Botswana and becomes quite distinct after seeing it couple times. You can confirm it's Botswana by the white back of the Google car, driving on the left, yellow outer lines, and the sun in the north.

The only other countries in Africa with that combination are:

  • Eswatini & Lesotho (but they will be hilly)
  • South Africa (though this is rare, as most of the coverage now is with blue back of the google car).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/botswana for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Bahia and Pernambuco pole markings
metas.note: Markings on poles are used by the electricity companies to identify them. This pole ID is long, yellow pole paint with a black code. The ones that start with a letter are found in Bahia and Pernambuco.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Black back of signs.
metas.note: If the landscape and vegetation make it look like you're in South America and you see signs with a black back, you're most likely in Brazil.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Blue water tanks
metas.note: Blue Fortlev water tanks are often seen on Brazilian roofs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Carnauba Palms
metas.note: Carnaúba palms have short but strong fan-like leaves, and a trunk that is smooth at the top and spiked at the bottom. They are commonly seen in Ceará, Piauí, and Rio Grande de Norte, but are also around the town of Xique Xique in Bahia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Ceará lamps
metas.note: Lamps in Ceará often have a fancy and colourful arm, whether as lampposts or attached to utility poles. It sometimes says the town on the arm.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Ceara pole top
metas.note: This asymmetrical concrete crossbar with no supports is exclusive to Ceara.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Coffee beans
metas.note: Coffee beans are by far the most common in Minas Gerais, but also can be found in Espírito Santo and northeastern São Paulo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Concrete bins
metas.note: Brazil often uses metal trash baskets outside houses. In Acre and Rondônia, however, it is much more common to see them made of concrete.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Espírito Santo - Exposed rock
metas.note: Espírito Santo, and the surrounding areas, often have large mountains with exposed rock.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Goiás pole markings
metas.note: Similar to the Bahia and Pernambuco poles, Goiás poles also use long, yellow pole paint with a black paint code, but it always starts with a number. They also have a rarer yellow on black pole ID, which can be either paint or a plate.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Maranhão wide insulators
metas.note: Poles with these wide insulators in a trident formation are common in Maranhão. The insulator itself is common across many states, but not in this configuration.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Mato Grosso pole
metas.note: Poles that have one insulator on top and alternating horizontal insulators can be found in Mato Grosso and southern Acre. It is also very rare in Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Paraná pines
metas.note: These distinct trees, called Paraná pines, have long horizontal branches with leaves only at the end. They grow mainly in the southern Brazilian states of Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Piauí road
metas.note:
Many roads in Piauí have red gravel on the side of the road. The gravel can appear spread above the tarmac shoulder or on roads with curbs.

NOTE: This can appear elsewhere. Use with caution.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Pole
metas.note:
The most common poles in Brazil resemble a ladder at the bottom. They are rectangular, with long segments at the base and small holes near the top. Chilean poles look similar but have 1–2 larger sections at the bottom instead of 3+ like Brazilian poles.

You might also find rounded concrete or wooden poles in Brazil, but they are less common and can be used for region-guessing within the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Road marker
metas.note:
A blue road marker with the road number at the top and the kilometer at the bottom is common in Brazil. Sometimes, the first two letters of the road number can tell you the state you're in (unless it starts with "BR").

(If you zoom out on the map where you can guess and look at Brazil, you’ll see short two-letter abbreviations for Brazilian states.)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Rolling grassy hills
metas.note: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo often have rolling grassy hills.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Rural Roraima
metas.note: Rural locations in Roraima are mostly open grassy plains with large, distant mountains in the background. Occasionally, you are on roads within the mountains. Furthermore, the grass in Roraima is distinctly thin, and grows in bunches.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Sugarcane plantations
metas.note: Sugarcane plantations are by far most common in the state of São Paulo, and are common in Paraná, Mato Grosso do Sul, and in the coastal north eastern states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Very tall grass
metas.note: Very tall grass can be often seen in the centre of the country, most notably in the Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia, and Minas Gerais states.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/brazil.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Alternating pole top
metas.note: This style of pole top, featuring 3 large, alternating insulators shaped like upward-facing hooks, is a good clue for Bulgaria. This pole top is likely unique to the country.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bulgaria for more clues.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Small alternating hooks
metas.note: Most poles in Bulgaria have small, alternating hook-shaped insulators, which can also be found in other countries (mostly on wooden poles, like Latvia, North Macedonia, and a few others). However, if you see them on a concrete pole, you're most likely in Bulgaria. Try using other clues to confirm.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/bulgaria for more clues.

metas.name: Bulgaria - Town signs
metas.note: Town entry signs in Bulgaria have a simple white design and use both the Cyrillic and Latin alphabets. Like directional signs, the two lines of text are clear and visible even from a distance.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/bulgaria.

metas.name: Cambodia - House on stilts
metas.note: In Cambodia, wooden houses on stilts are very common. The walls are often made of vertical planks, and many homes have double or triple roofs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/cambodia.

metas.name: Cambodia - Poles
metas.note: Cambodia for the most part uses two types of poles: a concrete ladder (or "waffle") pole, where the compartments are not holes but just indents, and a round concrete pole with holes along its whole length and a peculiar pattern in the top part. You can also rarely find wooden and thin metal poles.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Cambodia - Unique car
metas.note: This back of the google car with white stripe on the left, and a yellow stripe on the right is unique to cambodia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/cambodia for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - 45° angle transformers
metas.note: Transformers on Prince Edward Island and Nova Scotia will be installed at a 45° angle relative to the road. On PEI, red numbers will usually be written on the side.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Alberta bollard
metas.note: Alberta has a unique black and white bollard that is often found at intersections. It has a cylindrical shape and two black bands that wrap all the way around. It is one of the most useful Canadian bollards to learn because it appears so frequently.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Checkboard sign
metas.note: This diamond-shaped T-intersection "checkboard" sign is unique to Canada.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Concrete barriers
metas.note: British Columbia predominantly uses concrete barriers instead of guardrails.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Manitoba bollards
metas.note:
Manitoba uses black and grey painted bollards. Most of the time an orange stripe will be present below the grey one.

Wooden, rectangular bollards of this form are typically found further north in Manitoba

NOTE: Bollards in this format with just a black top are seen in Manitoba and Saskatchewan.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Manitoba stop signs
metas.note: You can sometimes find a green and white striped sticker on signposts in Manitoba.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Newfoundland bins
metas.note:
Bins made of wood planks can be seen on Newfoundland driveways. These are most commonly octagonal, however they can have other shapes.

NOTE: Although they are most common in Newfoundland, they can also sometimes be seen in other provinces, such as New Brunswick.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Newfoundland fire hydrant markers
metas.note: Fire hydrants in Newfoundland often have a diamond-shaped marker next to them.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Newfoundland T-intersection sign
metas.note: Newfoundland T-Intersection signs feature a rectangular yellow border around the diamond shape.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario diamonds
metas.note: You can find these diamond-shaped markers on the sides of the roads in Ontario. The colours can vary.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario guard rails
metas.note: In Ontario, you will often see these types of guardrails. They consist of cylindrical wooden posts, held together by precisely three metal wires. Some posts are marked by a reflective white band.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario speed signs
metas.note: Ontario speed limit signs may feature a black section at the bottom, with the words "km/h" or "begins" written in white.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Ontario traffic cones
metas.note: Ontario uses distinct orange and black striped traffic cones.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec double sign post
metas.note: Double sign posts on warning sings in Canada is unique to Quebec.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec guardrail bollards
metas.note: Quebec has unique bollards that are always attached to guardrails. They are long, thin white poles with a red or green reflector at the top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec pole stickers
metas.note: Québec poles may sometimes have a vertical black and yellow label. There is a small ‘Q’ in the black part.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec rectangle markers
metas.note: You can find these rectangular markers on the sides of the roads in Québec. The colours can vary.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Quebec stop sign.
metas.note: Stop signs with the word ‘Arret’ are unique to Quebec in Canada.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Sask stop sign white triangles.
metas.note: Those white triangles(can be different ammount of them) on signposts of stop signs are unique to Saskatchewan.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Sask white dashes between lines
metas.note: Those white dashes between yellow lines are most commonly found in Saskatchewan. You can also sometimes find them in BC but the landscape will be way different.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Saskatchewan alternating insulators
metas.note:
Pole top insulators in Saskatchewan alternate. While one pole will have one insulator on the left and two on the right, the next will have two on the left and one on the right.

NOTE: This can rarely be seen in Manitoba.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/canada for more clues.

metas.name: Canada - Transformers facing the road
metas.note: The transformers on poles will face the road in British Columbia and New Brunswick, while in other provinces, it will be parallel with the wires.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Canada - Wooden post pyramid top
metas.note: In Newfoundland and Labrador, most wooden posts on guardrails have this pyramid shaped top. Occasionally, you can spot them on standalone posts and signposts as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/canada.

metas.name: Chile - All yellow lines
metas.note: Within the Americas, all-yellow road lines are essentially unique to Chile. These lines are typically seen in National Parks or areas of high snowfall, as Chile usually uses all-white lines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/chile for more clues.

metas.name: Chile - Empty slot under sign
metas.note: Chile signs commonly have those empty slots at the top of signposts.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Chile - Pole
metas.note: Chile uses square concrete poles with an indent on both sides. They are somewhat similar to Brazilian poles, however have fewer horizontal supports in the indent. The upper part typically has small pinholes.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/chile.

metas.name: Christmas Island - Unique car
metas.note: If you see a Street View car with only the bed of a silver pickup truck visible, you know you're on Christmas Island.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/christmas-island for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - Antioquia pole paint
metas.note: These pole markings with one short black strip on the top and bottom, and a longer yellow section in the middle, are most commonly found in the Antioquia department. Sometimes, you can find them in the Cordoba department as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - Colombian cross
metas.note:
Signposts in Colombia are made of white thin metal and have a distinct cross on the back.

In the photo, green checkmarks show the "real" Colombian cross, and red X's show the ones that aren't right.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/colombia.

metas.name: Colombia - Yellow plates
metas.note:
In South America, yellow license plates are almost exclusive to Colombia. Commercial vehicles in Colombia may have white plates.

  • Images and descriptions courtesy of Plonkit.net
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/colombia.

metas.name: Croatia - Bollard
metas.note: Croatian bollards are white with a black rectangle and a red or white reflector. From the top, they are shaped like a triangle. Hungarian bollards are similar, but the black part with the reflector is positioned further from the top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/croatia for more clues.

metas.name: Curacao - Unique car
metas.note:
This black Street View car with a roof rack is unique to Curaçao.

It also has white sticker on front left/back right of roof rack.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/curacao for more clues.

metas.name: Czechia - Arrow-shaped signs
metas.note: Czechia uses arrow-shaped directional signs with a filled in tip. Due to the shape, they are recognizable from behind.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Bollard
metas.note: Bollards in Czechia have orange double reflectors on the front and a single white reflector on the back, with rarer blue and red variants. The same design is also found in Slovakia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Denmark - Bollard
metas.note:
Denmark's bollards are white with a yellow reflector and a distinctive dark orange stripe at the top.

Belgium's bollards are similar but have a rectangular reflector and no orange stripe at the top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/denmark.

metas.name: Denmark - Piped signs
metas.note: This signpost, where the pipe frame is bent around the sign, is unique to Denmark.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/denmark.

metas.name: Denmark - Street name ending - vej
metas.note: Most Danish street names end in "vej," which means "street" in Danish. Street signs typically have a blue background with white text.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/denmark.

metas.name: Dominican Republic - Unique car
metas.note:
A Street View car with a white front and a roof rack filled with thick black rubber stripes is unique to the Dominican Republic. Only the capital Santo Domingo and the Northern city of Santiago de los Caballeros are covered.

With this landscape - similar cars can be found in Guatemala and Curaçao, but they lack the thick black stripes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/dominican-republic for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Bollard
metas.note:
Ecuador is one of the countries in South America that uses bollards extensively, making them quite common in the country. There are two main types of bollards:

  • A round bollard with two red stripes
  • A flat bollard with two red reflectors on black

While other types of bollards can be found, they almost always follow the same color scheme and style.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Ecuador - Ecuador shitcam
metas.note:
If you have vibes that you are in South America and coverage was taken using "shitcam" camera you gonna be in Ecuador. There is "shitcam" in other countries but in South America you can only find "shitcam" in Ecuador.

Note: Ecuador also has GEN3(and little bit of GEN4) coverage not only shitcam! So don't discard Ecuador if it's not shitcam.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ecuador for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - Bollard
metas.note:
Round bollards with a rectangular reflector on the front and two circular reflectors on the back, which can be either white or orange, are common. Latvia's bollards might look similar, but they have a "half-circle" or flat curved shape, and sometimes feature numbers on them.

  • Baltic/Nordic bollard infographic
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/estonia for more clues.

metas.name: Estonia - Street name ending - tee
metas.note: In Estonia, the words for street and road are "tänav" and "tee," respectively. If you see street signs ending in "tee" or "tn" (with "tänav" often abbreviated as 'tn'), you know you're in Estonia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/estonia.

metas.name: Estonia - Street name ending - tn
metas.note: In Estonia, the words for street and road are "tänav" and "tee," respectively. If you see street signs ending in "tee" or "tn" (with "tänav" often abbreviated as 'tn'), you know you're in Estonia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/estonia.

metas.name: Eswatini - Vibes
metas.note:
Eswatini’s landscape is characterized by green, wooded hills and tall golden grass. Poles are made of dark brown wood and have a simple design, with insulators mostly mounted on the side.

You can confirm it's Eswatini by the white back of the Google car, driving on the left, yellow outer lines, and the sun in the north. The only other countries in Africa with that combination are:

  • Lesotho (which has bare, treeless mountains)
  • Botswana (which is super flat)
  • South Africa (though this is rare, as most of the coverage now is with blue back of the google car).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/eswatini.

metas.name: Finland - Street name ending - tie
metas.note: Street signs in Finland typically have a white background with black text, and most street names end in "tie."
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/finland.

metas.name: France - Blue sticker
metas.note: Small blue rectangular markings on utility poles are unique to France. They are often referred to as ‘stickers’ by the community, but are actually small plates.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Bollard
metas.note: The French bollard is extremely recognizable and appears very often. It is a round white post with a pointed top and a reflector band going all the way around. The band can be grey or red. Some rare variations have a fully red top. A bollard that is commonly found in Scotland looks similar, but has a blunt top instead of a pointed one.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/france.

metas.name: France - Ladder Poles
metas.note:
In France, these concrete ladder poles are pretty common. They're called "ladder" poles because of its similarity to the steps of a ladder.

NOTE: Spain can have the same poles, try using landscape or language to tell them apart.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/france for more clues.

metas.name: France - Road Numbers
metas.note: Small yellow signs displaying the road number, which typically starts with a “D”, are unique to France. They are commonly placed on top of directional signs or town entry signs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/france.

metas.name: France - Weird roadlines
metas.note: These middle road lines, where each dash consists of two offset blocks, are unique to France. They are not extremely common, but when you see them, you can safely guess France.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/france.

metas.name: France - Word for street - RUE
metas.note: The French word for street is “rue”. Street signs with "rue" can also be found in Belgium.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/france.

metas.name: Germany - Bollard
metas.note:
Germany uses these black and white bollards, with white and light-grey reflectors. The reflector will be orange on bollards next to intersections. They sometimes have plates containing the road number, and potentially other useful information. Many bollards also feature blue attachments on the side.

NOTE: Many European countries have similar bollards, however most will have different coloured reflectors. Luxembourg uses almost identical bollards, but they have 3 bolts instead of 2 on the reflector.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/germany.

metas.name: Ghana - Unique car
metas.note: All regular road coverage in Ghana features a unique Google car with a visible roof rack and a piece of black tape on the right end of the front bar. The hood is usually visible, displaying a Street View car wrapping with a red rectangle and other distinctive elements.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ghana for more clues.

metas.name: Gibraltar - Gibraltar silver tip antenna
metas.note:
That long antenna with a silver tip on google car is mostly found in Gibraltar.

It's British Overseas Territory so you will see a lot of English, UK license plates(back yellow, front white) but remember that Gibraltar drives on the right.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Bollard
metas.note:
Greek bollards are wedge-shaped with almost square reflectors, being red on the front and white on the back.

Andorra bollards are similar but landscape/vegetation will be way different most of the time.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Greece double white lines
metas.note: In Greece you will commonly see slightly faded, solid white double middle lines. This can be used to distinguish it from most other Mediterranean countries.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/greece.

metas.name: Greece - Greek harp pole
metas.note: These distinctive poletops, which have a metal frame shaped vaguely like a harp, are unique to Greece.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Greek lamps
metas.note: Poles in Greece are usually wooden and often will have this lamp with round shade above the light bulb. (You can sometimes find similar lamps in Serbia/North Macedonia so use other clues to confirm it's Greece)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/greece for more clues.

metas.name: Greece - Greek language
metas.note: The Greek language features a unique alphabet not used in any other language. It shares similarities with both the latin and cyrillic alphabet, however the lower case letters generally have softer shapes than the cyrillic letters.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/greece.

metas.name: Greenland - Vibes
metas.note: Coverage in Greenland was taken with many different vehicles. Architecture and landscape look very similar all over Greenland but it's hard to put it in words but it's pretty recognizable that's why I included it in this map.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Guam - Unique car
metas.note:
The entire Google car is blurred, however an antenna at the front right and a tiny part of the roof rack can be seen. You can confuse it with:

  • Puerto Rico(Cars there won't have front plates, signs will be Spanish).
  • Northern Mariana Islands(Antenna there will be noticeably closer to the camera but as long you will go Guam/NMI and not Puerto Rico you will get good score.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/guam for more clues.

metas.name: Guatemala - Unique car
metas.note: This gray Street View car with a visible roof rack and mirrors is unique to Guatemala. Don’t confuse it with the Dominican Republic car, which has black stripes on the roof rack, or the Curaçao car, which has a black front. A similar car is found in Laos, so always check the surroundings before making a guess.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/guatemala for more clues.

metas.name: Hungary - Bollard
metas.note:
Hungarian bollards are black-and-white, wedge-shaped, and typically have a red reflector at the front, and a white reflector at the back. (Croatian bollards are similar but the black part with reflector is closer to the top).

Note: Can appear in slovakia
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/hungary.

metas.name: Hungary - Holey pole
metas.note: Concrete holey poles with medium-sized holes going all the way to the bottom are common. They are similar to those in Poland and Romania, but Polish poles have holes that don't go all the way to the top or bottom, and Romanian poles are usually wider and painted white at the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/hungary for more clues.

metas.name: Hungary - Kilometer markers
metas.note: These green kilometre markers can be seen along most Hungarian roads.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/hungary.

metas.name: Iceland - Bollards
metas.note: Iceland's yellow bollards with a white reflector are unique and extremely common, found on almost every section of rural road across the country.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/iceland.

metas.name: India - Assam pole top
metas.note: Trident poletops with the tip of the middle bar bent at a 90° angle can be found in Assam.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Assamese language
metas.note: Assamese, mainly found in Assam, also uses the Bengali script, with the addition of some characters, most notably ৰ and ৱ.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Bihar pole paint
metas.note: Pole paint consisting of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes can be found in Bihar.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Bihar tree paint
metas.note: In Bihar, and less commonly Jharkhand, you may find trees with four red and white stripes painted near the bottom.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Flat Guna tiles
metas.note: Flat Guna tiles is just a tiled roof full of staple-shaped tiles. It can be found around Prayagraj, south east of Uttar Pradesh state,
metas.footer: From India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Flat tiles
metas.note: Flat tiles seem to be the worst type of tile by their appearance. They are mainly found in Madhya Pradesh and southern Uttar pradesh.
metas.footer: From India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Gujarat holey poles
metas.note: Concrete holey poles are unique to Gujarat and the Union territory of Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Guna tiles
metas.note:
It has “U” shape but there is a flatter shaped tile connecting tiles to each other.

It’s very common in southeastern Uttar Pradesh, western Bihar and rarely in northeastern Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.
metas.footer: From India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Indent poles
metas.note: Poles divided in two sections, in a similar fashion to Brazilian poles, are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Kannada Language
metas.note: Kannada is found in Karnataka and has a script with a lot of smooth curves and small circles. Many characters also feature a distinct squiggly tail in the top right corner, which is less common in Telugu. It is very similar to the Telugu script(but that one has usually "checkmarks" on top of letters.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Kerala yellow marking
metas.note: You can commonly find those small yellow pole markings in Kerala. Other states might have sometimes yellow markings like that but they are just way more rare.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Madhya Pradesh pole
metas.note: Poles in Madhya Pradesh often have a metal bar shaped like an upside down A slightly below the top of the pole.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Malayalam language
metas.note: The Malayalam script can be found in Kerala and mostly consists of somewhat simple-looking curvy letters, often containing upside-down U-shapes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Manipur metal trident pole top
metas.note: In Manipur you can often find trident poletops on poles made entirely out of metal. They sometimes have small bars on the top of the trident.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Marathi language
metas.note: Marathi, found in Maharashtra, also uses the Devanagari script so basically looks like hindi but if you can see the letter ळ that means it's Marathi. Sometimes you won't see that letter so don't rule out Maharashtra.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Odia language
metas.note: The Oriya script is found in Odisha and has a curvy look, with many letters having wide semi-circles covering the top. Many letters have a distinct diacritic in the shape of a wide curve above the top of the letter. A useful mnemonic is that the shape of the characters resembles 💀 emoji.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Punjab electricity boxes
metas.note:
Electricity boxes what are mint green with small window-like squares are almost exclusive to Punjab.

You can rarely see them in Haryana
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Punjabi language
metas.note: Punjabi can be found in Punjab in northwestern India. While the script looks somewhat similar to Hindi, it can generally be differentiated by the softer shape of the letters and the horizontal bar being broken over certain letters. It also has some distinctly different features, such as the letters ਨ, ਲ and ਅ.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Tamil language
metas.note: The Tamil script is found in Tamil Nadu and has a distinct combination of curves, straight lines and 90° angles. Some letters also have diacritics shaped like dots.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Tamil Nadu paint
metas.note: Markings on poles and trees, consisting of one black stripe in-between two white ones, are common in Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Telugu language
metas.note: Telugu, found in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh has script with a lot of smooth curves and circles. It looks similar to Kannada language but you can see a lot of distinct "checkmarks" on top of the letters.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: India - Trapez pole top
metas.note:
A connector on the pole which looks like an upside down trapezoid is most common in Chhattisgarh and somewhat common in Meghalaya, Tripura and Maharashtra, but can rarely be found in many other states.

NOTE: They can also be paired with Holey Poles in Gujarat and Ladder Poles in Andhra Pradesh, thus only use the trapezoid when no other pole meta is present.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/india.

metas.name: India - Upside down triangle pole
metas.note: Upside down triangle poletops placed below the top of the pole are commonly found in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and less commonly in Madhya Pradesh.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/india.

metas.name: India - Wide W tiles
metas.note:
This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.

It is very common in West Bengal, eastern Jharkhand and eastern Bihar, but doesn’t go further north than Purnia, Bihar.
metas.footer: From India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Window pole top
metas.note: Small metal poletops in the shape of a window are found in Punjab(super common) and Haryana.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/india for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Bali vibes
metas.note: Architecture in Bali is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism. The most important thing to look for crown-like roof pinnacles, found everywhere in Bali. Guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common too. Andesite, a dark, volcanic rock, is a common building material in Bali. You can often see gates, walls, and other intricately carved ornaments built from this material.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/indonesia.

metas.name: Indonesia - Front Plates on Motorcycles
metas.note: Motorcycles in Indonesia have front licence plates, as opposed to other south-east Asian countries which do not.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/indonesia.

metas.name: Indonesia - License plate
metas.note:
Indonesian licence plates are black with white letters. The letters usually appear as three white sections through the blur.

Commercial vehicles use yellow licence plates.

Plates in newer coverage can be white too.

NOTE: Malaysian licence plates are also black, but generally have two white sections.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/indonesia.

metas.name: Indonesia - North Sumatra pole
metas.note: These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is even, but features uneven insulators with one on one side and two on the other.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Nusa pole
metas.note: On the Lesser Sunda Islands (“Nusas”), you can find poles with an extra long support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Indonesia - Red-white pole paint
metas.note: Many of the steel poles in Indonesia are painted black, and often feature the Indonesian flag colours on them (red and white).
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/indonesia for more clues.

metas.name: Ireland - Dashed yellow lines
metas.note: Yellow dashed lines like this are super common in Ireland. You can find sometimes similar lines in New Zealand so if you are not sure use other clues like landscape/vegetation etc.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ireland for more clues.

metas.name: Isle Of Man - Red strip license plate
metas.note: If you feel like you're in the UK or Ireland but notice a red strip on the license plates, you're in the Isle of Man.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Israel - Yellow plates
metas.note: If you see cars with yellow front and back license plates in the Middle East, you are in Israel.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/israel-west-bank for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Bollard
metas.note: Italian bollards are triangular in shape, white with a black top, and feature a red front and a white rear reflector. Albania and San Marino use the same bollards.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Italy - Guardrail endings
metas.note: Italian guardrails commonly end in this distinct shape. The guardrail gets flatter, wider, and it bends away from the road.(San Marino can have same guardrail ending)
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/italy.

metas.name: Italy - License plates
metas.note: A short license plate with a double blue strip on the front and a long plate with a double blue strip on the back is unique to Italy. Similar long plates with a double blue strip can be found in Albania and France, but the front plates won’t be short.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/italy for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Chubu Plate
metas.note: Chubu plate is super unique because of the rounded shape, you can spot it from far away.
metas.footer: Check out Plonkit plate infographic or detailed plate document for more info.

metas.name: Japan - Chubu triangle mount
metas.note: Transformers in Chubu are often attached with large triangle and horizontal bars.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Chugoku arrow
metas.note: You may sometimes find an orange arrow located above the top most pole plate in Chugoku.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Chugoku cross-shaped bar
metas.note: The transformers in Chugoku, which have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a full triangle, will have a long horizontal or short vertical insulator(s) at the end.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Chugoku plate
metas.note: Chugoku plates will have usually written Energia in latin and sometimes they will include logo.
metas.footer: Check out Plonkit plate infographic or detailed plate document for more info.

metas.name: Japan - Chugoku pole top
metas.note: This pole top is unique to Chugoku, there is similar version that are more thicc so make sure the pole top is thin like the one on the image.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Hokkaido Arrows
metas.note: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido(You can find similar rarely in northern prefectures of Japan)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Hokkaido Plate
metas.note: Hokkaido plate can be recognized by having a lot of numbers in rows of 2.
metas.footer: Check out Plonkit plate infographic or detailed plate document for more info.

metas.name: Japan - Hokuriku plates
metas.note: Silver horizontal plates with logo on the top right. NTT plates will be also horizontal(in Tohoku NTT plates are vertical, and only Tohoku plate is horizontal).
metas.footer: Check out Plonkit plate infographic or detailed plate document for more info.

metas.name: Japan - Kansai 120 stepdown
metas.note: These attachments with an approximately 120-degree angle can commonly be found on poles in Kansai.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Kansai pole top
metas.note: This tuning fork pole top, with a thin wire and horizontal bar below, is common in the Kansai region. Make sure it looks exactly the same with that little thing on the wires in the middle(idk how to call it lol)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Kansai reflector
metas.note: Tall reflector with washed colors is exclusive to Kansai region.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Kansai transformers
metas.note: The transformers in Kansai have either a straight or zigzag bar mounted on the bottom of a square. The transformer(s) will be mounted on the sides of that same square. (Tohoku transformers are mounted in similar way but the bar will be connected to top of the square)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Kanto plate
metas.note: Often silver and handwritten characters. Horizontal characters above three vertical digits.
metas.footer: Check out Plonkit plate infographic or detailed plate document for more info.

metas.name: Japan - Kanto tall hat insulators
metas.note: Those insulators are unique to Kanto region and are easy to spot. They have black "hat" on top of white insulator.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu bulky insulator
metas.note: Black meteor like looking insulator, from far might be confused with Kanto tall-black hat insulator but Kyushu one appears little more bulkier even from far.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu Plates
metas.note: Distinc logo(sometimes might be missing). Three numbers horizontally near the top, with 4 vertical characters below them on the right(1 kana and 3 numbers).
metas.footer: Check out Plonkit plate infographic or detailed plate document for more info.

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu transformers
metas.note: Transformers mounted opposite side of the pole with a straight bar mounted on the side of the pole with 3 insulators on one side at the end.(Okinawa has T shaped bar)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu/Okinawa guy wire
metas.note: Guy wires that look like paddle are unique to Kyushu and Okinawa.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Kyushu/Okinawa reflector.
metas.note: Protruding bumps, sometimes darker reflector in the middle. Can also be found in Okinawa.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Okinawa plates
metas.note: Plate with multiple numbers and lines in between them. Often will have more than 2 plates.
metas.footer: Check out Plonkit plate infographic or detailed plate document for more info.

metas.name: Japan - Okinawa Transformers
metas.note: Transformers mounted opposite side of the pole with a T shaped bar mounted on the side of the pole.(Kyushu has straight bar). Sometimes only 1 transformer is present.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Shikoku cross bar
metas.note: The transformers in Shikoku, which also have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a half triangle, will have “hat shaped” short horizontal insulators at the end.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Shikoku orange band
metas.note: These orange and black bands wrapped around poles can often be found in Shikoku.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Shikoku plate
metas.note: Distinct logo that you can remember since it has 4 dots representing 4 prefectures of Shikoku.
metas.footer: Check out Plonkit plate infographic or detailed plate document for more info.

metas.name: Japan - Shikoku reflector
metas.note: 6 small reflectors with a little strip "connecting" them in the middle.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Tohoku plate
metas.note: Silver horizontal plates with logo in top left. NTT plate will be vertical.(In Hokuriku all the plates will be horizontal)
metas.footer: Check out Plonkit plate infographic or detailed plate document for more info.

metas.name: Japan - Tohoku reflectors
metas.note: Gray/White and Gray/Yellow reflectors.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Japan - Yamaguchi guardrails
metas.note: Yellow guardrails are exclusive to Yamaguchi prefecture.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/japan for more clues.

metas.name: Jordan - Black car meta
metas.note: While driving on the right side, yellow outer lines with white middle lines are commonly found in Jordan, Israel, and the UAE. The black back of the Google car without an antenna can help confirm you’re in Jordan 100%.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/jordan for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - Follow car
metas.note: In some of the Kenya coverage, you will be followed by a grey Toyota SUV.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kenya - Unique car
metas.note:
If you see a snorkel on the Google car, you’re in Kenya.

However, the car is sometimes seen without it, so don’t rule out Kenya if the snorkel isn’t visible.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kenya for more clues.

metas.name: Kyrgyzstan - Unique car
metas.note: Kyrgyzstan can be recognized by the silver Google car with four visible bars. Coverage was done during winter, so trees often lack leaves, the landscape appears drab, and snow is visible in many areas.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/kyrgyzstan for more clues.

metas.name: Laos - Unique car
metas.note:
If you are in South East Asia with this roof-rack car you gonna be in one of 4 cities in Laos: Vang Vieng, Luang Prabang, Savannakhet, and Pakse.

Note: You can find similar car in Guatemala so look around before making a guess.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/laos for more clues.

metas.name: Laos - Vientiane
metas.note: All other Laos coverage was taken with unique google car but if you have a vibe you are in Thailand but you will see yellow plates, ppl are driving on the right etc you will be in capital of Laos - Vientiane.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/laos for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Bollard
metas.note:
Half-circle/flat curved shape bollards with a rectangular reflector on the front and two circular reflectors on the back are common. The reflectors can be white or orange, and sometimes these bollards have numbers on them.

Estonian bollards might look similar, but they have a rounded shape and will never have numbers on them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Electricity marker
metas.note: You can find these electricity markers in Latvia — they have a distinct shape with a black tip and a different color underneath.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Hook pole
metas.note: Wooden poles with alternating pattern of hook-shaped insulators are really common in Latvia. They might appear sometimes in other countries but if you see them with flat landscape you gonna be most likely in Latvia(If you vibe baltics). Always try using other clues to confirm it.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Latvia - Street name ending - iela
metas.note: The Latvian word for street is "iela." This word is unique to Latvian, so if you see a street sign with it, you can be sure you're in Latvia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/latvia for more clues.

metas.name: Lesotho - Landscape
metas.note:
One of the best ways to identify Lesotho is by its characteristic ‘Lesotho mountains.’ These mountains are bare and treeless, often with tabletop-like shapes and recognizable horizontal rocky ridgelines.

You can confirm it's Lesotho by the white back of the Google car, driving on the left, yellow outer lines, and the sun in the north. The only other countries in Africa with that combination are:

Eswatini (the hills there have trees and usually tall golden grass around) Botswana (which is super flat) South Africa (though this is rare, as most of the coverage now uses the blue back of the Google car).
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lesotho.

metas.name: Lithuania - Bollard
metas.note: Lithuanian bollards are wedge-shaped with rectangular reflectors: an orange one on the front and a white one on the back.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lithuania.

metas.name: Lithuania - Street name ending - g.
metas.note:
The Lithuanian word for street is "gatvė," often abbreviated as "g." on street signs. If you see a street sign ending in "g.," you're likely in Lithuania.

This word is almost entirely unique to Lithuanian, though very rarely, you might see "gatve" (abbreviated as "gat.") in the Latvian capital, Riga.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/lithuania.

metas.name: Luxembourg - Bollard
metas.note:
Bollards in Luxembourg are black and white, wedge-shaped, and feature grey reflectors. Some have a distinctive indent in the lower half.

They look very similar to German bollards, with the main difference being that the reflectors on German bollards are attached with two bolts, while those in Luxembourg have three.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/luxembourg.

metas.name: Luxembourg - Yellow license plates
metas.note:
Luxembourg uses long yellow plates with a blue strip on the left. Since Luxembourg is a small country, foreign cars with white plates are somewhat common.

There are only a few other European countries that use yellow plates for private vehicles:

  • The Netherlands has yellow plates front and rear.
  • The UK has yellow rear plates.(driving left in UK)
  • Some pre-2009 French cars have yellow rear plates.
  • Danish commercial vehicles have yellow plates front and rear.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/luxembourg.

metas.name: Malaysia - Alam Flora bins
metas.note: Trash bins with this logo featuring a sunny landscape, saying ‘Alam Flora’ are found in Pahang, Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya. The logo will occasionally be absent, and it will just say ‘Alam Flora’.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Malaysia - Black sticker
metas.note: Electricity poles in mainland Malaysia often have black stickers on them, which can have different designs but are always black with white text and sometimes other elements. These stickers are quite distinct, so if it looks like you're in Southeast Asia, it's worth checking the poles for them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Boomerang lamp
metas.note: This lamp post with a supporting piece of sheet metal resembling a boomerang is found in Sarawak.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Malaysia - Directional Signs
metas.note: This is a typical Malaysian directional sign. Green background and hexagonal yellow highway shields are unique to Malaysia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Malaysia - Double white middle line
metas.note: Malaysia frequently uses double white center lines on its two-lane roads, making it the only Southeast Asian country to do so.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Malaysia - Isolated rock formations
metas.note: These isolated rock formations, rising abruptly from an otherwise flat landscape, can be found near the Thai border in Perlis state.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Malaysia - Johor yellow street signs
metas.note: Yellow street name signs are specific to the state of Johor.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - License plate
metas.note:
Malaysian licence plates are black and generally have two white sections. These are visible even when blurred.

NOTE: Indonesian licence plates are also black, but they will have three white sections.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Perlis and Kedah bins
metas.note: Trash bins with a logo resembling leaves are found in Perlis and Kedah.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Malaysia - S logo bins
metas.note: Trash bins with a logo resembling an ‘S’ are found in the states of Negeri Sembilan, Malacca and Johor.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Sabah pole
metas.note: Thin metal poles with two parallel pole tops are exclusive to the Sabah region of Borneo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Malaysia - Sarawak pole
metas.note: Electricity poles on the Borneo side typically have a 2-1 insulator configuration, and a long diagonal wooden support. They are exclusive to the Sarawak region of the island.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Stop Signs
metas.note: Berhenti stop signs are exclusive to Malaysia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malaysia for more clues.

metas.name: Malaysia - Thick Yellow Bars
metas.note: These thick yellow bars are also almost exclusive to Malaysia. NOTE: You can very rarely see similar patterns in Hong Kong.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/malaysia.

metas.name: Malta - Vibes
metas.note: If you see a license plate with a blue strip while driving left with this climate/landscape, you know you're in Malta. If you can't see the driving direction, use other clues like limestone rock walls to recognize Malta.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malta for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Agave salmiana
metas.note: Agave salmiana, also known as pulque agaves, have wide, smooth, curling leaves, and a crown-like appearance. They are common in the central Mexican valley and further north around the city of San Luis Potosi.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Agave tequilana
metas.note: Vast fields of blue agave (Agave tequilana), used to produce tequila, are mostly found in Jalisco and Nayarit.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Blindingly white soil
metas.note:
Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.

NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Blue Myrtle Cacti
metas.note: The Blue Myrtle Cacti have short arms that uniformly curve and point upwards. It is abundantly found in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Bollard
metas.note: These small, cylindrical white bollards with a black base are unique to Mexico. A yellow reflector is sometimes seen, as well as a flat version.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Boojum trees
metas.note: Boojum trees can be recognized by their alien, tentacle-like appearance. They are almost exclusively found in the southern half of Baja California.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Brittlebush
metas.note: Brittlebush are small shrubs with bright silver-grey leaves that are most commonly found in Sonora, especially around Hermosillo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Chihuahua cross
metas.note: A thick cross can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Cobblestone pavement
metas.note: This style of cobblestone pavement, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Concrete hanging insulator pole
metas.note: These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Guanajuato extremely dark fields
metas.note: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Hexagonal tiles pavement
metas.note: This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Kilometer marker
metas.note: Mexican kilometer markers are black-rimmed white signs mounted at hip height, featuring the 'km' text and the kilometer number, both in black, arranged vertically.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Light coloured rock walls
metas.note:
These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.

Comment from Vincent: When not in the sun, the rock walls appear darker, but it's likely the same type of rock.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Nayarit bollard
metas.note: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Oaxaca pavement
metas.note: This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is exclusive to Oaxaca.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Octagonal pole
metas.note:
Most utility poles in Mexico are made of CONCRETE and have an octagonal shape. Sometimes you can find them in Colombia so use different clues to make your guess.

If you see METAL octagonal pole you most likely will be in Philiphines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Oil palm plantations
metas.note: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Red agricultural fields
metas.note: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Rounded electric counter
metas.note:
Mexico uses those circular electricity counters.

You can find those in other countries:

  • Philippines(vegetation,climate will be different)
  • USA(looks different,English instead of Spanish etc)
  • Guatamela(has car meta)
  • Dominican Republic(has car meta)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Saguaro Cacti
metas.note: The Saguaro Cacti can be spotted in the western half of Sonora, featuring short curving arms that stem from a main trunk.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mexico - Thick Arrows
metas.note: In Mexico, arrows on signs are noticeably thick compared to other countries in the Americas.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mexico for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Wooden hanging insulator pole
metas.note: The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/mexico.

metas.name: Mongolia - Unique car
metas.note:
Gen4 Mongolia coverage was taken with two unique pickup trucks:

-White-Blue themed pickup truck mostly found only in Capital

-Pickup truck with a tent on top
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Mongolia - Unique car
metas.note: The Street View car with a tent on top is unique to Mongolia. While Mongolia has other unique Google cars, this is the most common one.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/mongolia for more clues.

metas.name: Namibia - Pickup truck
metas.note:
Namibia is the newest African country with coverage featuring the white pickup truck.

The landscape is similar to Botswana—flat and dry. Roads typically have yellow outer lines, and driving is on the left side.

Note: You may not always be on main roads with outer yellow lines. In such cases, it can resemble some parts of Kenya, which also drives on the left and sometimes features the white pickup truck.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/namibia for more clues.

metas.name: Netherlands - Yellow plates
metas.note: If you see yellow license plates on both the front and back in Europe with a super flat landscape, it’s likely the Netherlands. Luxembourg also uses all-yellow plates but is much hillier. Denmark may have yellow plates for commercial vehicles, so use other clues like architecture, bike lanes, and surroundings to confirm it’s the Netherlands.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/netherlands for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Bollard
metas.note: New Zealand has a unique white bollard with a red strip that wraps around the entire back and part of the front.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Give way sign
metas.note: Give-way signs in New Zealand have a white border and red text, while in Australia, give-way signs use black text.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/new-zealand for more clues.

metas.name: New Zealand - Marlborough possum guard
metas.note: Most utility poles in the Marlborough region have a long square shaped olive-brown possum guard. These can appear alongside the usual shorter silver possum guards.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: New Zealand - Timaru orange sticker
metas.note: Poles near Timaru often have a tall rectangle of orange paint on them with the text “DANGER LIVE WIRES”.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/new-zealand.

metas.name: Nigeria - Police follow car
metas.note: In Nigeria, Street View coverage often includes a police escort car visible "behind" the Street View car. However, it may sometimes be missing, so don’t rule out Nigeria if you don’t see it.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/nigeria for more clues.

metas.name: Northern Mariana Islands - Unique car
metas.note:
The entire Google car is blurred, but an antenna at the front right can still be seen. It will feel noticeably closer to the car than in other countries with a similar car.

You can confuse it with:

  • Puerto Rico(Cars there won't have front plates, signs will be Spanish).
  • Guam (You should be able to see little part of roof rack but as long you will guess NMI or Guam and not Peurto Rico you will get good points)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/northern-mariana-islands for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Bamboo snow poles
metas.note: Bamboo snow poles are regional and can mostly be found in Innlandet, Akershus, Østfold, Buskerud and Vestfold but can also be found rarely in Trøndelag, Vestland, Agder, Telemark and Rogaland.
metas.footer: Taken from Norwegian snowpoles by tobetelogi

metas.name: Norway - Green Plates
metas.note:
In Norway, commercial plates are green. These can often be seen on vans or big trucks(not semi-trucks).

NOTE: Within Europe, green licence plates are most commonly seen in Norway, but can also be found on electric vehicles in several other countries.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Long outer lines
metas.note:
If you see long dashed outer lines, you'll know it's Norway. You can find similar dashed lines with the same climate in Sweden, but they will be half the length, and Finland uses full outer lines.

(N)orway for normal, (S)weden for short, and (F)inland for full.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Long yellow-orange middle lines.
metas.note: Many larger roads in Norway have solid outer lines and yellow middle lines. The yellow lines have a distinct tinge of orange, making them easily recognizable.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/norway.

metas.name: Peru - Black yellow stripes
metas.note: Black-and-yellow stripes on guardrails are common throughout Peru. Similar striped guardrails can also be found in Bolivia, but to differentiate them, check the outer stripe. Peru uses a black stripe, while Bolivia features a yellow one.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/peru.

metas.name: Peru - Concrete blocks
metas.note: Signs with concrete blocks at the bottom are unique to Peru in South America.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Electricity counter
metas.note: Peru's electricity meters are rectangular and have horizontal rectangular openings. They look kinda like post boxes.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Sign post
metas.note: Black-and-white signposts like this are only found in Peru in South America. (If the signpost is inside a city, take this rule with a grain of salt, as you can rarely find them in other countries.)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Concrete roads
metas.note: If you're in Southeast Asia and see concrete roads, you're most likely in the Philippines, Thailand, or, much more rarely, Indonesia. If you're driving on the right side, it will be the Philippines, while driving on the left side indicates Thailand or Indonesia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Octagonal metal poles
metas.note:
Octagonal metal poles are quite common in the Philippines.

NOTE: They can sometimes be found in Bangladesh and some parts of Malaysia as well.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/philippines.

metas.name: Philippines - Trikes/Tuk-Tuks
metas.note: Tuktuks and Trikes are an extremely common sight in the Philippines. In many areas, they are more common than cars.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Philippines - Yellow and white lines
metas.note: Center lines in the Philippines can be white or a (usually slightly orange-tinted) yellow. The combination of the two colors, which you can also often get, is not really a thing anywhere else in Southeast Asia and as such is a good indicator for the Philippines.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/philippines for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Bollard
metas.note: Polish bollards feature a red strip that wraps around the entire bollard, with a red reflector on the front (sometimes hard to see) and a white reflector on the back. They may also have numbers on them. (from Plonkit)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/poland for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Holey pole
metas.note: Holey poles with smaller holes are common in Poland. Similar poles can be found in Hungary and Romania, but in Poland, the holes don't extend all the way to the bottom or the top.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/poland for more clues.

metas.name: Poland - Town signs
metas.note: Polish entering town signs have green background and white text with distinct font.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/poland.

metas.name: Portugal - Bollards
