metas.note: Portuguese bollards are either wedge-shaped with a noticeably thin white top, or flat with a wide reflector. While most reflectors will be white, you may also find orange reflectors. These are noticeably darker than the yellow reflectors in Spain.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Chevrons
metas.note:
Portuguese chevrons are black with yellow arrows.

NOTE: Portugal is the only Mediterranean country with this chevron colour scheme.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Portugal - License plate
metas.note: Old Portuguese license plates have a yellow strip on the right side. New plates follow the standard EU design without the yellow strip.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - No hunting signs
metas.note: Hunting signs with a red and white color scheme are commonly seen in rural areas of Portugal. They can be either diamond-shaped or rectangular.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Portugal - Pole
metas.note: Concrete ladder poles with very tall ladder steps are common in Portugal. Each step often has a small see-through hole.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/portugal for more clues.

metas.name: Portugal - Side walks
metas.note: Cobblestone sidewalks made of distinctly bright stones are very common in Portugal.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Portugal - Word for street - RUA
metas.note:
The Portuguese word for street is ‘Rua’.

NOTE: In Galician, the word for road is ‘Rúa’, with an accent on the ‘u’.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/portugal.

metas.name: Qatar - Car meta
metas.note:
Qatar's landscape is predominantly desert, with arid, mostly flat expanses of sand as far as the eye can see. You will often not see many trees or other greenery.

The Google car will usually be blurred, with only the antenna on the left and a sliver of the car visible. Sometimes the entire white pickup truck can be visible.

You might occasionally confuse it with the UAE or Oman pickup truck coverage, but in those countries, the antenna on the pickup car will be in the middle.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/qatar for more clues.

metas.name: Reunion - Unique car
metas.note:
Réunion's Street View car features visible side mirrors, a roof rack, and black tape at the end of the rear right bar.

Don’t confuse this with the Ghana car, which has tape on the front right bar.
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - Holey pole
metas.note: Concrete holey poles with wide holes and usually painted white at the bottom are common in Romania. They are similar to poles in Poland and Hungary, but Polish poles have smaller holes that don’t go all the way to the bottom or top, and Hungarian poles typically have smaller holes as well.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Romania - KM Marker
metas.note:
Within Europe, those red/blue/white KM markers are unique to Romania, the color representing the color the road will show up on the map.

How to use:

On the side is the road number and usually on the front are two cities, the first one is the closest largest city and the second one is the closest town.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/romania for more clues.

metas.name: Russia  - Bollard spam
metas.note: Near intersections in Russia you will commonly see a very large number of bollards.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/russia.

metas.name: Russia - Black sock sign post
metas.note: White signposts painted black at the bottom are very common in both Russia and Kazakhstan. However, Kazakhstan's entire coverage was done with a pickup truck, making it easy to rule out, indicating you're in Russia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/russia for more clues.

metas.name: Russia - Eastern bollard
metas.note: This unique very thin type of bollard that is attached to a stick is almost exclusively found in eastern part of Russia (east of Omsk +/-). Russia has a lot more different designs of bollards that you can find anywhere(even in eastern part)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/russia for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - Blue plates
metas.note: Blue license plates in Africa are unique to Senegal, sometimes you might find license plates that looks like standard europe license plate.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Senegal - French infrastructure
metas.note: Senegal used to be French colony so you will see similar ladder poles/bollards/lines that you would normally find in France.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/senegal for more clues.

metas.name: Serbia - Bollard
metas.note: Serbian bollards might look like Austria/Slovenia bollards but reflector will be always off-center. They have couple other designs but reflector will be always off-center.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/serbia for more clues.

metas.name: Singapore - Road marking: HUMP AHEAD
metas.note: Warnings are often written on the road in large letters, such as the famous “HUMP AHEAD”.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/singapore.

metas.name: Singapore - Street sign
metas.note: All street name signs in Singapore follow this unique format. They are green, with rounded edges and a distinct white font.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/singapore.

metas.name: Slovakia - Blue directional signs
metas.note:
Slovakia uses blue directional signs, with small white arrows.

This is mostly tip to differentiate it from Czechia which uses arrow-shaped signs.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Bollard
metas.note: Slovakian bollards have orange double reflectors on the front and a single white reflector on the back, with rarer blue and red variants. The same design is also found in Czechia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovenia - Bollard
metas.note:
Slovenian bollards are white with a black top, featuring a bright red reflector on the front and a white reflector on the back.

Austria uses similar bollards, but the back reflector is usually black rather than white.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/slovenia for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Bird nests pole top
metas.note: Big bird nests on top of poles are commonly seen in the northern part of the Northern Cape Province.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Bird Pole
metas.note: The most common type of pole in South Africa features 1 to 5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators that resemble rows of birds, which is why they are referred to as “bird poles” in the community.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-africa.

metas.name: South Africa - Blue back of google car(GEN4)
metas.note:
If you see blue back of the google car with/or without antenna you can be only in South Africa or Europe.

With yellow outer lines and driving left you are gonna be only in South Africa.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - KwaZulu trident pole top
metas.note: Trident pole tops are almost unique to KwaZulu-Natal.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - WC pole top
metas.note: Poles with 3 bars forming the letter ‘A’, with the bottom insulators being attached at the edges of a horizontal bar, can be found almost exclusively in Western Cape, and rarely in bordering provinces.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Africa - Yellow Outer Lines
metas.note:
In South Africa, most paved roads have single yellow outer lines and white center lines. This can be used to differentiate from Australia which has only white lines and never single yellow lines.

REMEMBER:

  • The Middle East can also have single yellow outer lines, so use driving side to tell them apart (South Africa drives left)
  • Botswana, Eswatini and Lesotho also use single yellow outer lines (but they usually have a white car)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-africa for more clues.

metas.name: South Korea - Jeju vulcanic rocks
metas.note: Jeju is a volcanic island that has a lot of rock walls, made of dark volcanic rocks.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/south-korea.

metas.name: South Korea - Language
metas.note: Korean script is highly distinctive, featuring a combination of circular shapes and blocky, straight-line characters.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-korea for more clues.

metas.name: South Korea - Pole marking
metas.note: Black and yellow diagonal stripes on poles are common in South Korea. You might confuse them with Taiwanese ones, but in South Korea, the stripes never go all the way to the bottom, while the ones in Taiwan usually do and have more of an orange tint to them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/south-korea for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Aragon Bollards
metas.note:
In Aragón, it is common to see this bollard design on regional roads.

It has a simple design, consisting of a short flat rectangular white stick with a grey reflector on both sides.

NOTE: There are similar bollards in other regions, but they appear much less frequently than in Aragón.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Asturias snow poles
metas.note: Yellow snow poles with one or two reflectors are unique to Asturias. They are usually found in the south of the region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Bollard
metas.note: Standard Spanish bollards have a yellow-orange reflector on the front and two white dots on the back, though the back can sometimes be blank. They are typically hollow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Catalan language - carrer
metas.note:
If you're in Spain and see a street sign with "Carrer" instead of "Calle", you're likely in a Catalan-speaking region, such as Catalonia, Valencia, or the Balearic Islands.

Andorra also uses Catalan as its official language.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Cogersa bins
metas.note:
Trash containers in Asturias frequently have the logo of COGERSA, the logo’s shape is distinct and can be recognized from afar.

NOTE: Recycling bins can also feature this logo.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Extremadura bollards
metas.note: In the region of Extremadura, it is common to see the normal Spanish bollards with green tops. This bollard variant is exclusive to this region.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Ladder poles
metas.note:
In Spain, these concrete ladder poles can be found amongst other types. They're called "ladder" poles because of its similarity to the steps of a ladder.

NOTE: France can have the same poles, try using landscape or language to tell them apart.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - No hunting sign
metas.note: In rural areas of Spain, you will often find no hunting signs. There are two versions, both unique to Spain. One is a simple white sign with text starting with "coto" and ending in "caza." The other has a diagonally divided black and white background.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Pedestrian crossing sign
metas.note:
Spanish pedestrian crossing signs have 8 stripes. This is the highest number of stripes in Europe, and almost unique to Spain.

NOTE: The only other European country with 8 stripes is Andorra.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/spain.

metas.name: Spain - Road Markers
metas.note:
Spain has distinct road markers, easy to recognize being usually square and having colourful borders. The code on top is the number of the road.

NOTE:: The letter codes before the road number on these markers are often an important region-specific clue, check plonkit for all the code regions.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Spain - Yellow guardrail reflectors
metas.note:
Spain has yellow reflectors on rounded A-type guardrails.

NOTE: Belgium, Andorra and Gibraltar also have yellow reflectors. For a good overview of European guardrails, see this infographic.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/spain for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Gen4 low cam
metas.note: All the Gen4 coverage taken in Sri Lanka is low-cam(gen3 coverage in Sri Lanka is not low cam), the only two other countries with low-cam is Japan and Switzerland but they look different. You can recognize lowcam because of wide blur of the street view car and lower vantage point compared to normal camera.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Pole
metas.note:
Sri Lanka typically uses concrete utility poles. Two pole types are common and distinctive:

  • Square poles with small pinholes in the sides. These pinholes are limited to the top part of the pole.
  • Poles with large see-through holes in the lower half of the pole (“holey poles“). These poles are unique to Sri Lanka.

They also commonly have those 3 big insulators on top of the pole shown on the second image.

NOTE: The square poles with small pinholes can look very similar to those found in Thailand. However, in Thailand the pinholes extend all the way to the bottom of the pole.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka.

metas.name: Sri Lanka - Unique car
metas.note: In most Generation 3 Sri Lanka coverage, you will be able to see the front of the Google car partially through the blur. It appears as blue-white-red patches, reminiscent of the French flag, with the red patch usually being the most visually distinct.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sri-lanka for more clues.

metas.name: Sweden - Blue and yellow chevrons
metas.note:
Sweden is the only country in Europe whose chevrons have yellow arrows on a blue background.

NOTE: While very rare, yellow on blue chevrons also exist in Luxembourg.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Sweden - M letter sign
metas.note:
On smaller roads, it is common to see these blue signs with a large white M.

NOTE: Similar signs can be found in Norway, however the font is distinctly different. The middle point of the M extends to the bottom of the letter. There are no similar signs in Finland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/sweden.

metas.name: Sweden - Short outer lines
metas.note:
If you feel like you're in one of the Nordic countries and see short dashed outer lines, you're likely in Sweden. Norway uses long dashed outer lines, and Finland uses full lines. (N)orway for normal, (S)weden for short, and (F)inland for full).

Warning: Many countries in Europe might also use short or medium dashed outer lines, so be cautious.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/sweden for more clues.

metas.name: Switzerland - Low cam
metas.note:
All the coverage in Switzerland is taken with a low-cam. The only other two countries with low-cam are Japan and Sri Lanka, but they look different.

You can recognize low-cam by the wide blur of the Street View car and the lower vantage point compared to the normal camera.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/switzerland for more clues.

metas.name: Taiwan - Pole marking
metas.note: Black and yellow diagonal stripes on poles are common. You might confuse them with South Korea's, but in Taiwan, they are usually longer, extend all the way to the bottom of the pole, and have an orange tint to them.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/taiwan for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Concrete road
metas.note: If you're in Southeast Asia and see concrete roads, you're most likely in the Philippines, Thailand, or, much much more rarely, Indonesia. If you're driving on the right side, it will be the Philippines, while driving on the left side indicates Thailand or Indonesia.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Pole
metas.note:
Square poles with small holes running from bottom to top are distinctive to Thailand. In Sri Lanka, similar poles exist, but the holes are limited to the top part of the pole.

Note: You can find same poles in Laos(but Laos drives right and most cities coverage is done with google car with roofrack)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/thailand for more clues.

metas.name: Thailand - Sign Posts
metas.note:
Signposts in Thailand are square and bulky in shape, usually white, and often have the bottom painted black.

NOTE: In Southeast Asia, this design is unique to Thailand.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/thailand.

metas.name: Tunisia - Follow car
metas.note: A light green Toyota or dark green Mazda was escorting the Google car through most of Tunisia coverage, and if you look behind, you can almost always see them. Sometimes you won’t see it, so don’t rule out Tunisia if you can't spot the escort car.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/tunisia.

metas.name: Turkey - Bollard
metas.note: Turkish bollards are white and rectangular with a red reflector on the front, making them quite unique. Similar bollards exist in Romania but are very rare. Australian bollards typically have a reflector on the back and a slightly different design(also they drive left in Australia/NZ comparing it to Turkey)
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Turkey - Stop signs
metas.note: All stop signs in Turkey feature the text "DUR," making them unique to the country. No other country uses this stop sign.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/turkey for more clues.

metas.name: Uganda - Unique car
metas.note: Uganda's unique Google car is white with visible square mirrors, and its coverage is limited to Kampala. Some national parks in Uganda are covered with different cars, but these are quite rare.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/uganda for more clues.

metas.name: Ukraine - Red car meta
metas.note: A red Google car, with or without an antenna, in Generation 3 and on crappy roads is always Ukraine. However, the car may not always be visible, so don’t rule out Ukraine if you don’t see it.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/ukraine for more clues.

metas.name: United Arab Emirates - Silver car
metas.note: If you have vibes/other clues that you are in the middle east and you have silver car in Gen3 that means you can only be in UAE.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-arab-emirates for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - Scottish passing place signs
metas.note: These ‘Passing Place’ signs are unique to Scotland.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - UK license plates
metas.note: In the UK, license plates are white on the front and yellow on the back. In Ireland, both the front and back plates are white.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom for more clues.

metas.name: United Kingdom - UK road lines
metas.note:
These middle lines, that consist of long dashes with cat’s eyes (reflectors) in the gaps between the dashes, are a good clue for the UK.

Note: You can find it rarely in Ireland.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-kingdom.

metas.name: United States - Cali three stripes
metas.note: Utility poles with 3 yellow stripes are most commonly found in California.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Minnesota bridge signs
metas.note: In Minnesota, these yellow signs with vertical, black triangles are placed before bridges at most major river crossings and at the beginnings and ends of guardrail sections on large highways.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Montana/SD bollard
metas.note:
The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a white diamond reflector on top.

Montana tends to have 1 bolt on the reflector, while South Dakota tends to have 2.

NOTE: This is a common design and can be found in many states. Additionally, square bollards can be rotated on their side to look like diamonds. Use with caution.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Nevada bollard
metas.note: This bollard is found in Nevada. It consists of a reflector on a thin stick. The reflector is a vertical rectangle that consists of a white field surrounded by a black outline.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - No passing zone sign
metas.note: Yellow triangular signs with the text "No Passing Zone" are unique to the United States.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Saguaro Cactus
metas.note:
In US you can find this cactus(tall,thick upward-curving arms) south of Arizona.

You can find same cactus in Mexico over the border in Sonora or similar one in north of Argentina.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Square guardrail
metas.note:
You can find those square guardrails mostly in state of New York and Wyoming.

You can rarely see them in states close to New York state.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - Washington bollard
metas.note: The state of Washington uses bollards that consist of a white or brown post with a white rectangle on the front of the bollard, and two smaller white or silver squares on the back of the bollard.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/united-states for more clues.

metas.name: United States - West Virginia fraction signs
metas.note: West Virginia sometimes features street signs with a symbol that resembles a fraction inside a circle.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/united-states.

metas.name: Uruguay - Thicc white signs post
metas.note: In a lot of Uruguay coverage, the camera quality is somewhat smudgy and you will see black back of the google car. You will also commonly see thick white wooden signposts, which are typically painted white. They often have up to four rectangular notches at the back of the post.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.

metas.name: Uruguay - Trident poles
metas.note:
Uruguay uses a handful of different utility poles. One very common and useful one are the so-called trident poles, which get their name from their distinctive pole tops with three insulators that point upwards.

NOTE: These trident poles are not found in neighbouring Argentina and Brazil.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.

metas.name: Uruguay - Triple road lines
metas.note: Uruguay often has these triple road lines, that consist of double yellow roadlines with white dashes in between. This is a design not seen anywhere else in the Americas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.

metas.name: Uruguay - White bollards and stone barriers
metas.note: These white bollards, with one side often painted yellow, and stone barriers, are specific to Uruguay.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/uruguay.

metas.name: US Virgin Islands - USV unique car
metas.note: Car coverage on the islands will have a large, visible street view car, which will either be red or white.(Don't confuse it with Bermuda google car which is full black)
metas.footer: Check out https://www.plonkit.net/ for more clues.

metas.name: Vietnam - 75% holey pole
metas.note: Concrete poles with holes running up to 75% of the height of it are found almost exclusively in northern Vietnam. Note: there is poles that holes goes up to 50% of the height all over Vietnam.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - Bollards
metas.note: The most common bollard type is a small square concrete bollard that is painted white with a red top.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/vietnam.

metas.name: Vietnam - Central A-shape poletop
metas.note: Central A-shaped top is where you can see an A standing on the crossbar. It can be centered or off to the side. It is almost exclusively found in central Vietnam.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - Dalat green houses
metas.note: Greenhouses can be found in Đà Lạt valley.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - Dragonfruit plantations
metas.note: Dragonfruit plantations are most common in Bình Thuận, but can be found all over the south.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - Holey Poles
metas.note: Holey poles, with holes either only on the lower half or almost all the way to the top, are common in Vietnam.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/vietnam.

metas.name: Vietnam - North canals
metas.note:
Low-lying, agricultural plains sometimes accompanied with canals are common around Nam Định and southern Hanoi.

Note: You can also find canals max south of the country but they will have different landscape.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - One sided pole top
metas.note:
One sided top is where the pole has the crossbar on one side with a single diagonal support beam. It can either be completely on one side or uneven to one side. Important to note that you should not confuse it with trapezoid support which has an extra horizontal segment in the support beam.

It is almost exclusively found in the far south.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - Pepper plantations
metas.note: Pepper planations are most commonly found in Dak Nong, Dak Lak, and Gia Lai provinces.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - Plain concrete pole.
metas.note: Plain concrete poles without holes or pinholes are almost exclusively found in northern part of the country.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - Red white sign post
metas.note: Vietnam uses red-and-white striped signposts, and occasionally red-and-yellow ones.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/vietnam.

metas.name: Vietnam - Rubber trees
metas.note:
Rubber tree plantations are primarily found in the provinces to the north of Ho Chi Minh City, as well as in several parts of the Central Highlands.

Rubber trees can be recognized by their thin trunks. In Vietnam, it is typical for a section of the tree trunk to be wrapped in a piece of plastic. These trees tend to be neatly organized in a dense grid-like pattern.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/vietnam.

metas.name: Vietnam - Side mounted lamp
metas.note: Lamp mounted to the side of the pole with 2 brackets is only found in the region shown on second image.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - South Canals
metas.note: Canals are very commonly found in the Mekong Delta. Canals can also be found in the north, but the landscape is very different.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - Spools pole
metas.note: Mounted spools are spools mounted directly to the pole. It is almost exclusive to the far south of the country .
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - Traditional architecture
metas.note: Traditional architecture can mostly be found in the north, but can be seen in Đắk Lắk and Gia Lai. The landscape will generally be flatter in those two areas, which can be a good clue for that area.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - triangle supports
metas.note:
When two supports of the main crossbar of the pole form triangle it should put you south of the country.

There is similar support that looks like trapezoid so make sure it's actually triangle.

Note: I found those poles rarely north but there was always some other clue to know it's not south.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - tripple trapezoid pole
metas.note: Poles with 3 half trapezoid supports on a side are exclusively found in the North of the country.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.

metas.name: Vietnam - Ventilation electric box
metas.note:
Meter Box Designs with trap door style windows plus ventilation slits on the sides are very common in the province of Khanh Hoa. It can be found everywhere in the province from rural villages to coastal areas.

Note: Other regular Meter box designs can be found throughout the whole country.
metas.footer: Credit to Vietnam Doc , Vietnam pole document and VietnamCord.
